title: During an Earthquake
content: During an earthquake, remember the three essential actions: Drop, Cover, and Hold On. Drop to your hands and knees before the earthquake knocks you down. Cover your head and neck under a sturdy table or desk if possible. Hold on to the furniture until the shaking completely stops. If you are inside a building during an earthquake, stay indoors until the shaking ends. Stay away from windows, mirrors, glass doors, hanging objects, bookshelves, and heavy furniture that may fall. Never use elevators during or immediately after an earthquake because power failures may trap people inside. If you are outside during an earthquake, move to an open area away from buildings, streetlights, utility poles, trees, bridges, and power lines. Stay in the open until the shaking has completely stopped. If you are driving during an earthquake, slow down carefully and stop in a safe location away from bridges, tunnels, overpasses, buildings, trees, and power lines. Stay inside the vehicle until the shaking stops.
